title: Construction Business Plan: Build a 12 Month Plan
meta_description: How to build a 12 month construction business plan: set quarterly goals, pick the KPIs that track them, and keep the plan flexible enough to survive the year.
h1: Construction Business Plan: Build a 12 Month Plan
hero_subtitle: A practical guide to planning the year so the business moves in one direction.

intro.answer: A 12 month plan is a roadmap: what you want to achieve, how you plan to achieve it, and by when. Its real job is making sure everyone in the business is pulling the same way.

image.alt: A 12 month planner laid out for a construction business planning session

intro.roadmap: This guide covers what a 12 month plan is, why it matters for a construction business, what belongs in it, and how to build one that fits your business rather than a template.

briefing.title: Quarterly Goals Beat an Annual Wish List
briefing.intro: A year is too long a horizon to hold anyone to. The plans that survive contact with a real construction year break the twelve months into quarters, each with a number attached, and each with something that tells you early whether it is working.

panels.heading: What should a 12 month construction plan include?
paragraphs: Financial goals first: revenue, profitability, or cost reduction, set against realistic project estimates and market conditions rather than hope.

Then marketing strategy, covering how leads arrive and how clients are kept. Then project planning, assessed against the pipeline you can actually see. Then the people side, because a plan that needs a bigger team is not a plan until the hiring is in it.

panels.heading: Build it in this order
paragraphs: Break the year down rather than trying to write it in one sitting. Each quarter should be challenging and still attainable.
steps: Set specific, measurable goals for each quarter, using last year's data as the guide.
Pick the KPIs that will tell you whether each goal is on track.
Align every quarterly goal with where the business is meant to be in three years.
Review at the end of each quarter and adjust. The plan is not carved in stone.

review.label: Review quarterly
review.text: Market conditions move and so does the business. A plan you have never revised is not disciplined, it is out of date.
